A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same width-scaling study. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices support comparison. Identifiable inconsistencies in some v2 figures are document issues, not missing evidence.

before.justification: v1 reports original MLP and GPT training experiments, alignment measurements and linear-network simulations in Section 5 and Appendices C–F.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds image-dataset evaluations, Transformer comparisons and diagnostic results.

M1.justification: The SP, µP, SP-full-align, MUSOLI and refined coordinate-check procedures are retained. The output-layer initialization highlighted in v2 Section 5.2 already appeared in v1 Appendix B; its promotion does not establish a new method.

E1.justification: v2 adds Fashion-MNIST and Tiny ImageNet to the evaluated image-classification coverage, including loss and parameterization sweeps. MNIST, CIFAR-10, multi-index data and DCLM-Baseline remain. The separate Gaussian-noise streaming scenario in v1 Appendix C.4.3 is removed.

E2.justification: GPT comparisons gain SP-full-align with SGD and MSE-loss SGD configurations in v2 Figures F.6 and F.8. The SP/NTP/µP convergence comparison and full-network CIFAR-10 CE/MSE/MSE-plus-softmax comparisons in v1 Figures F.16–F.17 are removed. The principal parameterization families remain unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 revises Figure 2's RMS-alignment normalization and explicitly restricts instability-threshold searches to learning rates above the optimum in Appendix D.4. New SP trajectory tests use learning-rate multipliers 1, 1.9 and 2.1 in Figure C.3. Existing training budgets and the default single-epoch protocol are largely retained.

E4.justification: v1's convergence-to-limit study, including initialization, warmup and weight-decay analyses, is removed with Appendix C.4.3. Shallow CIFAR-10 loss ablations are also removed. v2 adds SP stability time courses, full SP-full-align GPT coordinate checks and Transformer loss/parameterization tests addressing the proposed stability mechanism.

E5.justification: v2's checklist newly defines error bands as empirical 0.025–0.975 quantiles from four seeds and identifies initialization and data randomness. Existing run counts are largely retained; the removed convergence study had reported 100-seed estimates and variability analyses. No general increase in repeated runs is established.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial result sets and exponent summaries, including Tiny ImageNet's SP-full-align optimal exponent of -1.45 versus a maximal-stable exponent of 0.0 in Table F.1. The AdamW/SP-full-align GPT results change from approximate transfer in v1 Figure F.6 to a shrinking optimum in v2 Figure F.7. Convergence-study and shallow CIFAR-10 results are removed.

T1.justification: v2 adds Definitions 1 and C.11 for learning regimes and maximal-stable learning rates, and corrects the alignment exponent in Section 3.1 from -1/2 to 1/2. Informal Proposition 2 drops bounded-loss assertions, although formal Proposition C.12 retains them. The principal proofs and scaling results are otherwise retained.

C1.justification: The central controlled-divergence and feature-learning claims remain. The abstract narrows prediction of optimal learning-rate exponents to prediction of maximal-stable exponents that guide optimal choices, and no longer claims that loss remains stable alongside gradients and activations.

C2.justification: v2 clarifies that nonvanishing updates are necessary but insufficient for useful feature learning, strengthens qualifications on predicting optimal learning rates, and explicitly leaves validation of the proposed initialization to future work. Appendix B expands practical implications, while Figure F.7 qualifies the earlier GPT transfer interpretation.

D1.justification: v2 supplies experiment-code and RCC-package links and states public availability, replacing Section 5's future-release promise in v1. The checklist adds A100/RTX 2080 Ti hardware and under-24-hour run-time information. These substantially expand documented reproducibility resources; external availability was not independently checked.

R1.justification: v2 adds discussion of Atanasov et al.'s related CE pseudo-catapult regime, expands finite/infinite-network and large-learning-rate references, acknowledges earlier RCC formulations, and supplies missing warmup citations. The central positioning relative to Tensor Programs and Everett et al. remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and contribution list are substantially rewritten. Appendix B gains an expanded practitioner discussion, Appendix F is reorganized by optimizer and scientific question rather than primarily by dataset, and a NeurIPS checklist is appended.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figure 6 and Tables C.1/F.1, expands Figure 7, and substantially rearranges appendix displays. It also introduces mismatches: an SGD-labeled panel appears in Adam Figure E.9, and Figure F.31 reuses SP-full-align panels despite its µP caption, replacing v1's distinct µP display.

improvement.justification: The added GPT loss comparison and broader image evaluations strengthen tests of the central explanation, while clearer organization, code-access information and defined error bands improve usability and reproducibility. The net gain is limited by removed supplementary evidence and new plot/caption errors in Figures E.9 and F.31; the bounded-loss assertion also persists in Appendix C.12 despite its removal from the main claims.
